evals.prompt: Build a React confirm-delete modal for our project list. Keep it simple.
evals.expected_output: Uses native dialog (or an accessible primitive) with aria-labelledby, initial focus on the safe action, Escape to close, focus returned to the trigger, specific button labels, and a polite announcement after deletion; notes what was tested.
expectations: Uses <dialog> with showModal() or a named accessible primitive rather than a hand-rolled div overlay
Dialog is labelled by its title (aria-labelledby or equivalent)
Focus returns to the triggering element when the dialog closes
Buttons name the action (e.g. 'Delete project' / 'Cancel'), not Yes/No
Focus ring uses :focus-visible and is not removed

evals.prompt:
Audit this signup form for accessibility:
Sign up
Invalid email
evals.expected_output: Reports findings with WCAG criteria and severity: missing labels (1.3.1/3.3.2/4.1.2), blocked paste (3.3.8), div button (2.1.1/4.1.2), error not linked or color-only (1.4.1/3.3.1), missing autocomplete (1.3.5); each with an exact fix; states that automated tools alone would not verify everything and lists what was not checked.
expectations: Flags placeholder-only inputs as missing labels and cites a WCAG criterion
Flags the blocked paste as a 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication failure
Flags the div used as a button and recommends a native <button>
Recommends linking the error with aria-describedby and aria-invalid
Recommends autocomplete tokens such as email and new-password
Each finding has a severity and one concrete fix

evals.prompt: Our design uses light gray #9CA3AF text on white for secondary labels. The designer says APCA says it's fine, so we're compliant, right?
evals.expected_output: Explains WCAG 2 contrast ratio (4.5:1 for normal text) is the compliance bar; APCA is not part of WCAG 2.x and not adopted in WCAG 3 as of 2026-09; #9CA3AF on white is about 2.5:1 and fails; suggests a darker token.
expectations: States WCAG 2.x ratios (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large) are the compliance requirement
States APCA is a secondary/perceptual check and not a compliance substitute
Concludes the pair fails AA for normal-size text
Suggests a darker color or token that reaches 4.5:1

evals.prompt: Can you make our page transitions feel snappier? They take about 600ms and use ease-in.
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is primarily motion tuning. Routes to or applies motion-design guidance (shorter duration, ease-out); may mention reduced-motion support, but does not run a WCAG audit.
expectations: Does not produce a WCAG conformance audit or checklist as the answer
Recommends shorter duration and an ease-out curve, or points to motion-design
